_comment: Models Comodor can download and run on this machine, with no network
afterwards. Adding one is an edit to this file: every interface reads it,
so a new entry appears in the terminal picker and the browser at once,
Every `size` and `sha256` here was read from the Hugging Face API, not
typed. They are not decoration: a download is refused unless the bytes
hash to what is stated, because a truncated model file is not obviously
broken — it loads, and then produces nonsense.
To add one: give it an `id` that will be its filename, a `name` people
read, an https `url` to the .gguf, the exact `size` in bytes and the
`sha256`. Everything else is optional and anything omitted is reported as
python -c "import json,sys;[print(f['rfilename'], f['size'], f.get('lfs',{}).get('sha256')) for f in json.load(sys.stdin)['siblings'] if f['rfilename'].endswith('.gguf')]"
`needs_ram_gb` is the working set, which is larger than the file: the
weights plus the context window plus room for the process. Understating
it costs somebody a download and a crash, so it is rounded up.

models.name: Qwen2.5 Coder 1.5B
models.description: The one to start with. Small enough to run on a laptop with no discrete graphics and still answer in a couple of seconds, and it was trained on code rather than adapted to it. Weaker at long reasoning than the 7B.

models.name: Qwen2.5 Coder 7B
models.description: The best balance for most machines. Handles multi-file edits and tool calls properly, which the smaller models do not. Wants 8 GB of memory free and is noticeably faster with a GPU.

models.name: Qwen2.5 Coder 14B
models.description: The strongest of these at code, and the slowest without a GPU. Worth it on a machine with 16 GB free and graphics; painful on anything less.

models.name: Llama 3.2 3B
models.description: A general model rather than a code one. Better than the coders at reading prose, explaining, and summarising a transcript; worse at writing a diff.

models.name: Phi-3.5 Mini
models.description: Small and unusually strong at reasoning for its size. A good second opinion when a coder model has talked itself into something.
